facts.statement: EVO operates a multi-location beauty network with CENTER, NORTH and SAIGON locations.
The normalized network contains 512 branch service records, 30 staff records and 813 exact service-to-staff relations.
The client product is configured for RU, EN and VI.
Online booking uses Altegio with an official-form fallback.
Recognizable brand anchors are the EVO wordmark, olive/deep-olive family, warm cream and restrained bronze accent.

inferences.statement: The breadth of services can create choice overload, so navigation should guide by goal/category and preserve context.
A multi-location network increases the risk of choosing the wrong branch, so branch state should persist through catalog, specialist and booking flows.
Beauty purchasing is strongly affected by perceived expertise, hygiene/safety, visual quality, specialist confidence and proof.

hypotheses.statement: Goal-led navigation and AI-assisted selection may reduce abandonment before booking.
A coherent premium visual campaign may increase perceived quality and trust versus inconsistent source-feed imagery.

objectives: Make a large catalog understandable in a few taps.
Keep branch, service and specialist context exact through booking.
Raise perceived brand coherence and premium quality.
Reduce uncertainty before the booking handoff.
Support Russian-speaking, English-speaking and Vietnamese users consistently.
weaknesses: large catalog can be cognitively heavy
public visual sources are not one consistent design system
commercialPriorities: repeat contact and future CRM continuity
